articles.title: The Telescope
articles.summary: This article details the construction of a highly portable 10-inch truss-tube Dobsonian telescope, introducing an innovative "beeswax trick" for creating rigid yet easily disassembled truss pole joints. The author elaborates on material choices, unique fabrication methods for lightweight components, and practical considerations for packing the instrument into a compact cube for travel. The design emphasizes portability and ease of setup for amateur astronomers, showcasing several clever solutions for building a travel-friendly telescope.

articles.title: Last Man on the Moon: A Visit with Gene Cernan
articles.summary: The article recounts the author's serendipitous encounter with Apollo 17 astronaut Gene Cernan, the last man on the moon, at the Naval Postgraduate School. The author describes the excitement of getting Cernan to sign his lunar globe and taking a photo, followed by attending Cernan's engaging speech. Cernan, an alumnus, captivated the audience with humorous anecdotes and profound reflections on his moon missions, space exploration, and the spiritual significance of his voyages.

articles.title: Through An Astronaut's Eye
articles.summary: This article, 'Through An Astronaut's Eye,' by Craig Wandke and David North, encourages amateur astronomers to adopt a unique perspective for lunar observation. It details the specific guidelines given to Apollo 8 astronauts for examining the Moon's surface, suggesting these criteria can enhance telescopic viewing. The piece outlines what to look for on impact craters, uncratered surfaces, rilles, and at the terminator, offering a structured approach to selenography.

articles.title: Observe The Very Inner And Very Outer Solar System
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for July, detailing how to spot various solar system objects including Jupiter, Saturn, Mercury, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, and asteroid 4 Vesta. It also highlights three eclipses occurring during the month, including a partial solar eclipse and a lunar eclipse, offering advice for finding challenging objects and emphasizing safety precautions for solar observation. The author encourages early risers and nighttime astronomers to observe these celestial events.

articles.title: Backyard Observatory on the Cheap
articles.summary: Denny Woolaghan details the construction of an inexpensive backyard observatory using a Rubbermaid storage shed. The project involved modifying the shed to create a roll-off roof, adding mobility with wheels, and raising the floor to an optimal viewing height using readily available materials like 2x4s, concrete blocks, and plywood. The article emphasizes affordability and DIY construction.

articles.title: Meteors
articles.summary: This article provides observing details for the 2000 Perseids meteor shower, including its connection to Comet Swift-Tuttle and predicted activity, despite a bright moon. It also highlights the eclipsing variable star Algol in the constellation Perseus, offering observation tips for its brightness minima. Additionally, the document includes information on subscribing to Sky & Telescope through the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), an upcoming SJAA Yosemite star party, and a telescope for sale.

articles.title: "Sky Show" Event Scheduled for Davis
articles.summary: Astronomy Magazine is organizing a "Sky Show" event in Davis, California, on August 4th and 5th, aiming to engage both the general public and expert amateurs. The event will feature keynote speakers, exhibits, family activities, solar viewing, and a large public star party with specialized observing stations for constellations, lunar/planetary objects, and deep-sky viewing. It also seeks volunteers and telescopes, and supports Davis's strong light pollution ordinance.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) maintains a loaner telescope program for its members, managed by Mike Koop. This article provides a status update on the program, detailing which telescopes are immediately available, currently on loan, or on extended loan, and lists a waiting list for popular scopes. SJAA members can contact Mike Koop to inquire about borrowing a telescope or to be placed on a waiting list.
